{{Quote|You'd need a twisted mind to design a Podracer the way Farwan & Glott did. But you'd need to be totally insane to actually fly one.|Anonymous Podracer pilot referring to Neva Kee|<ref name="IG">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref>}}
'''Neva Kee''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Xamster/Legends|Xamster]] [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who was active during the year [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Considered a daredevil, he was notorious for piloting a [[Farwan & Glott/Legends|Farwan & Glott]] [[FG 8T8-Twin Block2 Special|8T8-Twin Block2 Special]] Podracer, a vehicle that was known for the fact that the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] was not only attached to the [[Engine/Legends|engines]], but placed in front of them, making the vehicle considerably more dangerous than other Podracers. While considered to be insane by some, the Xamster was hailed as a revolutionary in the sport by others. With a cult following in tow, Kee went on to achieve fame on the jungle [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Baroonda/Legends|Baroonda]], and participated in several races on the planet of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Perhaps the most famous race Kee participated in was the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]], held annually near the Tatooine [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]]. The race would be Kee's last; during the final stretch of the second lap, Kee wandered off course and was never seen again.

==Biography==
===The Xamster from Xagobah===
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Xamster/Legends|Xamster]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Xagobah/Legends|Xagobah]], Neva Kee decided to risk his life for fame and fortune in the high-speed sport of [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]]. Kee purchased and flew a [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Farwan & Glott/Legends|Farwan & Glott]] [[FG 8T8-Twin Block2 Special|8T8-Twin Block2 Special]], an unorthodox craft with a [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] located at the front end of two massive engines. The FG 8T8 had no power couplings; the two engines were simply attached directly to the cockpit.<ref name="DB" /> This criticized configuration put [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] into a considerable amount of risk, although others hailed it as the next step in the sport's evolution.<ref name="IG" /> Despite the dangerous setup, the vehicle's compensation was its superior turning power and maneuverability.<ref name="Racer">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref>

Kee's rebellious image earned him a rabid following among nonconformist Podracing fans.<ref name="DB" /> Kee eventually took his career to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] planet of [[Baroonda/Legends|Baroonda]], which held several Podracing courses that moved through various kinds of terrain, ranging from dense jungles, ocean-side beaches, cities, and misty swamps. Kee personally excelled on [[Baroo Coast/Legends|Baroo Coast]], a track that made its way through a wide beachhead. Kee eventually achieved the crowd's favor on the course, and was considered a pro. With victories under his belt, Kee stepped up his game by traveling to numerous planets in the [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] racing season, including [[Ord Ibanna]], [[Aquilaris]], and [[Mon Gazza/Legends|Mon Gazza]].<ref name="Racer" />

===The Boonta Eve Classic===
{{Quote|Did Watto sell you that Podracer?|Neva Kee attempts to insult another pilot, at the expense of the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Merchant/Legends|junk dealer]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]]|translated=1|audio=NevaKee-taunt.flac|<ref name="Racer" />}}
[[File:NevaKee_Game.png|thumb|left|150px|Neva Kee on Tatooine]]
Kee eventually made his way to the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he partook in several races. One race which sped through the [[Hutt Flats/Legends|Hutt Flats]] pitted the Xamster against the likes of the [[Navior's species|beaked]] [[Navior|"Bullseye" Navior]], the gray-skinned [[Jinn Reeso]], and the [[Nosaurian/Legends|Nosaurian]] [[Clegg Holdfast/Legends|Clegg Holdfast]], among others.<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> Kee managed to survive, and went on to enter Tatooine's annual [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]], a race that attracted seasoned professionals and newcomers alike from the far reaches of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="tpm">{{Film|I}}</ref> The Boonta race was one of he longest races of the circuit,<ref name="Racer" /> stretching through miles of desert terrain. Kee's Podracer was placed in the fifth and last row on the outside pole position of the starting grid, giving Kee a shaky start. The opening ceremonies were hosted by the [[Troig/Legends|Troig]] race commentators [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fodesinbeed Annodue]], who introduced the pilots to the crowd. The race's host, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the]] [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] arrived shortly after and flagged the start of the race himself. With the Hutt's go-ahead, the pilots burst out of the starting grid and into the course, with the exception of two&mdash;the pilots [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Ben Quadinaros/Legends|Ben Quadinaros]] had both stalled. Skywalker was able to move off of the grid after reconfiguring his pod, and swiftly caught up to the rest of the pack.<ref name="tpm" />

Kee, despite having navigated the course so far with expertise, was nonetheless stuck in the rear of the pack near [[Wan Sandage/Legends|Wan Sandage]] and [[Dud Bolt/Legends|Dud Bolt]]. All three pilots were passed by Skywalker as they finished the opening stretch of the race which passed through [[Mushroom Mesa/Legends|Mushroom Mesa]]. As the race continued, the [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]] pilot [[Ratts Tyerell/Legends|Ratts Tyerell]] crashed in the [[Laguna Caves/Legends|Laguna Caves]] during lap one, stringing wreckage through the tight passageway. Kee managed to make it through and continued into the [[Canyon Dune Turn/Legends|Canyon Dune Turn]], only to find that native [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] were firing on the Podracers for sport. During the second lap, the Tuskens claimed the Podracer of [[Teemto Pagalies/Legends|Teemto Pagalies]]. Despite the growing number of wrecks, Kee was unable to move ahead in the pack.<ref name="tpm" /> Finally, during the last stretch of lap two, which passed over the [[Hutt Flats/Legends|Hutt Flats]], Kee flew his Podracer off course and disappeared, never to be seen again.<ref name="DB" /> Skywalker ended up winning the Boonta.<ref name="tpm" />

Although Kee's ultimate fate is unknown, if he had died, he would be one of only two casualties to have taken place during the race, the other being Tyerell, who had died during his wreck in the Laguna Caves.<ref name="tpm" /> The rest of the pilots who had wrecked survived their collisions to race another day.<ref name="PT">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref> [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], replicas of Kee's Block2 Special were sold to [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]].<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
[[File:NevaKee-AnakinsSpeedway.jpg|thumb|right|125px|Neva Kee, Xamster Podracer pilot]]
Neva Kee was an excitable individual who flew a daredevil Podracer. Due to how different his Podracer was built, he was considered to have something of a rebellious image, and as such garnered a following of like minded fans.<ref name="DB" /> However, critics cited the Xamster as being completely insane.<ref name="IG" /> Regardless of what anyone had to say, Kee never let the crowds get to him or disrupt his focus. As Kee gained further fame from his career on Baroonda, he eventually made his way to Tatooine for the famed Boonta Eve Classic. However, the race would become his last. It is not known what caused him to veer off course during the Boonta's second lap.<ref name="DB" />

A Xamster, Kee had bluish-green skin across the back of his body, his arms, and his head. This was offset by an off-white color that dominated his chest and abdomen, along with the inside of his ears and his lower jaw. Kee had red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and had a patch of off-white [[Hair/Legends|hair]] in the center of his chest. His back had blue colored spines that went down the length of it, along with some spines going down his stomach. He had small white horns or spines on the back of his head that jutted out at various angles. Xamster's were often short and Kee was no exception, standing at only 1.07 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="DB" />

==Skills and abilities==
Neva Kee had the mental resolve and quick reflexes one would need in order to pilot a Podracer, much less a Podracer which was renowned for its tight handling and furious accelerator.<ref name="DB" /> Kee's familiarity with the quirks of the Block2 Special granted him victories on Baroonda, most notably on the Baroo Coast course.<ref name="Prima" /> Kee headed to Tatooine for further tests of skill, and while he had survived at least one race on Tatooine, he somehow managed to disappear completely from the Boonta Eve Classic, and by extension, the rest of the sport.<ref name="DB" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|The unique, Y-framed FG 8t8 Twin Block2 Special has no tethers.|The [[Podracing Quarterly/Legends|''Podracing Quarterly'']] publication details Kee's Podracer|<ref name="YJCCG">{{YJCCG|set=Boonta Eve Podrace|cardname=Neva Kee|link=boontaevepodrace/light/large/13nevakeepodracerpilot.html}}</ref>}}
[[File:NaviorRacing.png|thumb|left|200px|Neva Kee, top, piloted his Block2 Special on Tatooine.]]
The most notable aspect of Neva Kee's career was his unique Podracer, a Farwan & Glott produced 8T8-Twin Block2 Special. The Podracer was cited as having more relation to a [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] than a Podracer, seeing that traditional Podracers consisted of engines attached to a cockpit with the use of cables and [[Energy binder/Legends|energy binders]]. The Block2 however ditched that concept for something different: A Podracer with no cables or energy binders at all, making for one solid vehicle. In addition, the Block2 had the oddity of having the cockpit placed in front of the engines, as opposed to behind it.<ref name="DB" /> As such, this made head-on collisions much deadlier. In addition, the Block2 was fairly frail, and could not suffer too much abuse from a course's terrain or the attacks of other pilots. Instead, the Block2 Special relied heavily on its otherwise superior mobility and traction to keep it in the race, unscathed.<ref name="Racer" />

Kee's Block2 was painted with a bright blue color that dominated the top of the pod, while the underside was silver in color. The engines also had white stripes that circled around them, as well as the front of the engines having more of a purple hue to them. The front of the cockpit was adorned with a symbol painted in white. When racing, Kee did not utilize headgear.<ref name="Racer" /> Instead, he just wore a [[Clothing/Legends|gold harness]]<ref name="YJCCG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Xamster_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|150px|During the pre-production stages of ''The Phantom Menace'', Terryl Whitlatch provided conceptual art for Neva Kee.]]
Neva Kee first appeared in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], as one of the Podracer pilots from the film's Podracing scene. The [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization of the film]] does not feature Neva Kee, instead introducing a character named [[Habba Kee]]. Habba Kee also appeared in the junior novel [[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker|''Star Wars Episode I Journal: Anakin Skywalker'']]. In both books, Habba crashes and is killed during the Boonta Eve Classic. In the film, Neva Kee appeared only as a low resolution computer-generated model that was used for distance shots of Kee's Podracer, despite a detailed maquette being built of the character as well several detailed illustrations from concept artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]], who originally used Kee's design for the pilot Wan Sandage.<ref name="IG" /> During the film, Neva Kee does not suffer Habba Kee's fate. In the revised [[Star Wars: Episode I The Beginning|rough draft]] of the script, Neva Kee is said to be from [[Aquilae]].<ref name="DB2">{{DB|organization|boontapodrace|Boonta Eve Classic Podracers}}</ref>

Neva Kee had a far more substantial appearance in the 1999 tie-in [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'', released for both the PC and [[Wikipedia:Nintendo 64|Nintendo 64]]. Kee was one of several playable characters, and he could be unlocked during the second circuit on the first track that took place on Baroonda. Kee is initially locked from players, but if they manage to win Kee's favored course, players can unlock his pod to race with. Kee is voiced by [[Peter Lurie]], who also voiced [[Boles Roor/Legends|Boles Roor]] in the game.<ref name="Racer" /> Kee was set to appear in ''Racer's'' [[2002]] sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'', as evidence by a number of pre-release screenshots. Kee was ultimately cut from the game. While not a part of the Podracing story mode, Neva Kee did nonetheless appear in the [[2012]] video game ''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''. Players could select his Podracer to race in for free races. Concept art created by [[Robert St.Aubin]] depicted Kee with much more piloting gear than he has been previously seen with.

Kee's Podracer appears on the cover of the junior novel ''[[Jedi Quest: The Dangerous Games]]'', written by [[Jude Watson]]. The cover depicts Anakin Skywalker piloting it. Neither Kee nor Kee's Podracer appear anywhere in the novel, however. While Skywalker does fly an old Podracer's vehicle, he actually flies Ratts Tyerell's [[Titan 2150 rocket engine/Legends|''Titan'' 2150]].<ref name="DG">''[[Jedi Quest: The Dangerous Games]]''</ref> During the release of ''The Phantom Menace'', [[Micro Machines Star Wars Action Fleet|Micro Machines]] released a die-cast toy of Neva Kee's Podracer.
